comparison: Perfect alignment on GDNF overexpression rescue phenotype (C2, C25-C31, C34-C37, C39). Both evaluations find the data convincingly supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and multiple independent markers; peer reviewers describe the approach as 'careful and unbiased' without raising concerns.

Strong alignment on bulk RNAseq identification of EOMES (C3, C40-C44, C46, C48, C50-C53). Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval validates the systematic approach and statistical thresholds; peer reviewers accept this as part of the unbiased discovery process leading to EOMES+ cell identification.

Partial overlap on EOMES+ cell characterization. OpenEval R3 covers immunofluorescence characterization (C54-C63) with minor reservation about mechanistic validation of PLZF's indirect regulation. Peer R1 covers broader identification including lineage tracing (C3-C5, C54-C75) and finds the identification 'convincing' without challenging the immunofluorescence data.

Strong alignment on lineage tracing experiments (C64-C75). OpenEval finds the confetti reporter system provides 'strong evidence for SSC identity' with rigorous design. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'convincingly identify' EOMES+ cells with 'functional characteristics of SSC,' accepting the lineage tracing data.

Strong alignment on busulfan challenge experiments (C76-C84). OpenEval supports the well-designed experiment showing busulfan resistance and regenerative capacity. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the 'functional characteristics of SSC' that are 'convincingly demonstrated' without raising concerns.

Critical disagreement on proliferation/slow-cycling claims (C6-C8, C85-C89). OpenEval supports the EdU data showing differential proliferation but notes the proliferative exhaustion model is 'inferred rather than directly demonstrated.' Peer reviewers explicitly question whether data 'convincingly show' slow-cycling and require removal of this terminology, indicating the proliferation data does not definitively establish this characteristic.

Strong alignment on scRNAseq heterogeneity analysis (C9, C90-C119). OpenEval finds the comprehensive analysis with quality metrics well-supports heterogeneity conclusions. Peer reviewers explicitly state the data 'support the growing realization that the spermatagonial As population is heterogeneous' and accept this as a significant contribution.

Strong alignment on differential gene expression in scRNAseq (C120-C124). OpenEval supports the findings but suggests reporting FDR values would strengthen claims. Peer reviewers accept these data as part of the 'careful and unbiased' approaches supporting heterogeneity, without challenging the differential expression findings.

Strong alignment on ID4/EOMES relationship (C128-C134, C137-C138, C141-C144). OpenEval finds the antibody validation and quantitative overlap data well-supported with reasonable conclusions about transgene limitations. Peer reviewers recommend additional analysis comparing EOMES in ID4 bright/dim cells as enhancement rather than correction, indicating acceptance of presented findings.

Strong alignment on background/contextual claims about GDNF and SSC biology (C1, C17-C21). Both evaluations accept these well-established, citation-supported background claims that provide scientific context. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong alignment on historical context and literature review (C10-C16). Both evaluations accept these citation-supported background claims. OpenEval notes they 'accurately represent the cited literature'; peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging the contextual framework.

Strong alignment on PLZF background (C22-C24). Both evaluations accept these citation-supported claims establishing rationale for studying PLZF. No concerns raised by either evaluation about the background context.

Strong alignment on marker background information (C32-C33, C45, C47, C49). Both evaluations accept these citation-supported contextual claims about various markers. OpenEval notes they establish significance of RNAseq-identified genes; peer reviewers accept the contextual framework.

Alignment on speculative/technical limitation claims (C103, C105, C139). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are 'explicitly speculative' and 'untested hypotheses' appropriately presented. Peer R10 supports these as accepted technical considerations and caveats, while peer R12 also accepts the speculations as reasonable.

Alignment on speculative statements (C139, plus C89 in OpenEval R6). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting speculation. Peer reviewers accept these as reasonable possibilities that don't affect core findings, without challenging the speculative nature.

Strong alignment on prior literature context (C125-C126, C135-C136, C140). Both evaluations accept these citation-supported claims from published work providing context for EOMES/ID4 relationship interpretation. No concerns raised.

Partial alignment on mechanistic model and PLZF regulation (C7-C8, C63, C145, C150-C151, C154). OpenEval supports the model as reasonable given data, noting exhaustion is inferred by analogy. Peer reviewers accept PLZF regulation of EOMES+ cells as a 'significant contribution' but their critique of 'slow-cycling' terminology suggests some reservation about the exhaustion mechanism, though they don't explicitly challenge the regulatory relationship.

Alignment on background claims in mechanistic model (C146-C149, C152-C153). Both evaluations accept these citation-supported contextual claims about PLZF function and hematopoietic analogies. OpenEval uses these to support the inferred exhaustion model; peer reviewers accept the background framework.

Strong alignment on high-level summary claims (C4-C5, C9, C75). OpenEval finds these well-supported by collective experimental data from lineage tracing, busulfan, and scRNAseq. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the identification of EOMES+ cells with SSC characteristics and heterogeneity findings as 'convincing' and a 'significant contribution.'

Alignment on heterogeneity summary claim (C9). OpenEval supports this as well-supported by multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly state the data 'support the growing realization' of heterogeneity and plasticity in spermatogonial populations.

Minor overlap on technical observation (C62). OpenEval notes EOMES+ cells detected in Id4-/- mutants support inference about PLZF's indirect regulation. Peer R10 accepts this as a technical consideration without challenge, consistent with acceptance of overall findings.
